Q1: The rest of the work (filtering the "Expected files" list against `files_touched` and listing out-of-scope tests separately) cannot touch `scripts/` under this heal issue. How should it be delivered?
Choices:
A. Do the filtering inside the scope (RECOMMENDED). In the "Build implementation context" step of `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, take the output of the `expected-files` call at line 2729 and pass each path through `files_touched_scope_guard.py`, the same way `implement_prepush_test_gate_narrow_allow_list` does at lines 562-568 (`--issue-body-file`, `--issue-number`, `--issue-meta-file`, `--pipeline-login`). In-scope paths print as before. Out-of-scope paths go under a separate "the scope guard will refuse edits to these; report the conflict instead" line. If the guard is unavailable, the current output stays. Add a regression test under `tests/` that runs that step logic on an issue body whose `files_touched` leaves out `app/tests/test_x.py`. The script itself stays unchanged. This adds shell logic to a workflow file covered by the 480,000-byte size guard.
B. Treat the issue as delivered. The prompt-level rule from PR #9860 already tells the editor that Expected files is not a scope, and to report out-of-scope conflicts instead of editing them. The re-plan answers "Files likely to change: None", so implement closes the issue through its success-no-op path. The script-side filter is dropped.
C. Close this heal issue with no further changes (as in B), and have a maintainer open a new non-heal issue whose `files_touched` covers `scripts/implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh` and `tests/test_implement_prepush_test_gate.py`. That issue makes the filter change in the script, as suggested fix 1 originally described. This needs a person to file the new issue.
